source.title: Northern Whig, 6 June 1958, p. 3 ("Unionists top poll in Newtownabbey"); Belfast News-Letter, 17 May 1961, p. 5 ("Voting likely for two Derry seats")
source.publisher: Northern Whig (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: returned without a poll: the Northern Whig's polling-day report says 'polling took place for the Dungiven division of Londonderry County Council', not Faughanvale (6 June 1958, p. 3), and the Irish News of the same date heads its result 'Dungiven Division. (Only seat contested)' (p. 1). John M'Laughlin is named as the outgoing Faughanvale member in the 1961 nomination report (Belfast News-Letter, 17 May 1961, p. 5), so he held the seat.

note: Polled 5 June 1958 (Belfast News-Letter, 21 May 1958: 'polling will take place on June 5'). Nominations were received on 20 May. Seventeen seats were returned unopposed at nomination. Two contests were nominated, Dungiven and Faughanvale, but polling on 5 June took place only in Dungiven; the Faughanvale poll did not go ahead and John M'Laughlin, who is named as the outgoing member in 1961, was returned (Northern Whig, 6 June 1958, p. 3; Irish News, 6 June 1958, p. 1). The Dungiven result is recorded here. No party labels were printed for the unopposed returns. The nomination report of 21 May 1958 had listed the outgoing member James Donaghy and John M'Laughlin as contesting Faughanvale; no Faughanvale result was ever printed, and the poll went ahead only in Dungiven. Returned unopposed.
